title: Extension bounds for Frobenius modules
statement:
Let $0\to V'\to V\to V''\to 0$ be an exact sequence of Frobenius
modules. If $V'$ and $V''$ are mixed of weights at most $w$, then
$V$ is mixed of weights at most $w$.

proof.text: Write the maps as $f:V'\to V$ and $g:V\to V''$, and the three automorphisms as $F',F,F''$. Thus $f$ is injective, $g$ is surjective, $\operatorname{im}f=\ker g$, $Ff=fF'$ and $gF=F''g$. By [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] choose stable filtrations $0=A_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq A_m=V'$ and $0=C_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq C_n=V''$, with pure successive quotients of weights $a_i\le w$ and $c_j\le w$. The coefficient field, $q$, and $\iota$ are the same for both filtrations.

source.place: entire proof: pull back and splice the two stable filtrations

proof.text: Define $W_i=f(A_i)$ for $0\le i\le m$ and $W_{m+j}=g^{-1}(C_j)$ for $0\le j\le n$. These definitions agree at $m$, since $f(A_m)=\operatorname{im}f=\ker g=g^{-1}(C_0)$. Images and inverse images preserve inclusions, so this is increasing. Its endpoints are $W_0=0$ and $W_{m+n}=g^{-1}(V'')=V$. This includes $m=0$ or $n=0$.

source.place: entire proof: pull back and splice the two stable filtrations

proof.text: Each subspace is stable with equality, as required by [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. On the left, $F(f(A_i))=f(F'(A_i))=f(A_i)$. On the right, equivariance and $F''(C_j)=C_j$ give $F(g^{-1}(C_j))\subseteq g^{-1}(C_j)$. Conversely, for $x\in g^{-1}(C_j)$, put $y=F^{-1}x$; then $g(y)=(F'')^{-1}g(x)\in C_j$, so $x=F(y)$ belongs to $F(g^{-1}(C_j))$.

source.place: entire proof: pull back and splice the two stable filtrations

proof.text: For $1\le i\le m$, the map $A_i/A_{i-1}\to W_i/W_{i-1}$ sending $[x]$ to $[f(x)]$ is well-defined and linear. Every target class has such a representative, so it is surjective. If $f(x)\in f(A_{i-1})$, choose $z\in A_{i-1}$ with $f(x)=f(z)$; injectivity gives $x=z$, proving its kernel is zero. It is therefore an isomorphism. The quotient actions defined in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] satisfy $[f(F'x)]=[Ff(x)]$, so this isomorphism commutes with Frobenius.

source.place: entire proof: pull back and splice the two stable filtrations

proof.text: For $1\le j\le n$, the map $W_{m+j}/W_{m+j-1}\to C_j/C_{j-1}$ sending $[x]$ to $[g(x)]$ is well-defined and linear. Given $z\in C_j$, surjectivity of $g$ supplies $x\in V$ with $g(x)=z$, and then $x\in g^{-1}(C_j)=W_{m+j}$. Its kernel is zero, because $g(x)\in C_{j-1}$ is precisely $x\in g^{-1}(C_{j-1})=W_{m+j-1}$. Thus it is an isomorphism, and $[g(Fx)]=[F''g(x)]$ proves Frobenius compatibility for the quotient actions in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].

source.place: entire proof: pull back and splice the two stable filtrations

proof.text: If $e$ is either of these isomorphisms, an eigenvector $x\ne0$ of the source quotient with eigenvalue $\alpha$ maps to the nonzero eigenvector $e(x)$, since $e(Fx)=F e(x)$ and $e(\alpha x)=\alpha e(x)$. Applying the same argument to $e^{-1}$ gives equality of eigenvalue sets. Consequently each left graded piece of $W$ is pure of weight $a_i$, and each right graded piece is pure of weight $c_j$, by the eigenvalue definition of purity in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. Concatenate these weight lists, all bounded by $w$. The filtration constructed above now satisfies every clause of that node's definition of mixedness, proving the assertion. Zero graded pieces cause no exception, since they have no nonzero eigenvectors.
